work.title: Dispatch plane unavailable: dispatcher ticks fail with launch timeouts and the claude runtime drops every launched session, so no worker, reviewer or approver session can run

judgement.reason: Real, severe availability work, not covered by anything open or delivered. Evidence (all readable on the control plane): dispatcher failed 3+ consecutive ticks (last failed 2026-10-06T13:41:49Z, last success 13:41:12Z) with every launch ending 'The operation was aborted due to timeout'; since 09:51Z every session launched on vishrog ended 'vanished: the claude runtime ... has not reported session/pane' within 13-45s (sessions on GY-1363/1364/1365/1366); doctor report gap since ~10:14Z. The checkout confirms the gap the item names: autonomy.ts abandonLaunch covers only approver/escalation launches (lines 414/424/636/650) and no fail-fast bound that fails a stuck launch as its own action with a runtime-naming fault exists on the dispatch path (src/daemon/cycle-dispatch.ts launch(), src/master/launch.ts launchStartMs/SessionStartError). Not fixed by a delivered item: GY-1369 (commits 20e3b4716b, 9466be0b61) delivered only the confined-PID liveness fix and the operations.md loop-down runbook; GY-1370 only the namespace-aware pid probe — neither restores the runtime nor hardens launches. No open item overlaps: GY-1292 is docs word budget, GY-1365 the revert approver App, GY-1371 releasing-diagnoses, GY-1372 intervention attention. Priority 0 because dispatch-plane availability gates every item — the moment the open human-gated items (GY-1292, GY-1365) unblock or any new fault files, nothing can be launched, and recovery needs the operator or the GY-1369 runbook plus the launch-path hardening to stop one dead runtime silencing dispatch plane-wide.

criteria.text: The dispatcher completes a full tick with a successful launch again: the next requested session launch is claimed and acknowledged inside the 2-minute launch bound, and master status no longer raises the plane-unavailable fault on dispatch (no 'failed N ticks in a row' line, 'The operation was aborted due to timeout' gone).

A launched worker session stays reported by its runtime through at least one lease renewal — no 'vanished: the claude runtime on vishrog has not reported session … absent from 2 consecutive session reports' within 5 minutes of its last observed activity — verified across two consecutive post-recovery dispatches.

A launch that cannot be acknowledged within its bound fails its own dispatch action with a fault naming the dead runtime instead of timing out the whole tick, and the doctor cadence resumes (no gap greater than one hour between doctor runs).
